title: Hosted Canary Rollouts (Hosted routes) — GA Launch Brief (working)
body:
Doc status: Working launch brief for internal alignment. Not customer-facing. Please leave comments inline.

Last updated: 2025-03-20 (Soojin)

---

1) Summary

We are taking the existing rollout primitives (model versioning, fallback routing, observability) and shipping a GA “Hosted canary rollout workflow” for percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes.

What GA means here:
- Customers can create and execute canary rollouts in Console for Hosted routes with a step plan (e.g., 1% → 5% → 25% → 50% → 100%).
- Guardrails are enforceable and visible (max step size, minimum soak time, approval gates, and auto stop/rollback based on SLO signals).
- Deterministic cohorting ensures stable splits and debuggability.
- Customers can see a timeline/activity log and baseline vs canary metrics comparisons.

Non-goals for this GA (explicitly communicate internally to avoid scope creep):
- Multi-armed bandits / dynamic traffic optimization.
- Automated quality eval gating as a hard block (we can support optional manual quality metrics and follow-up automation).
- Dedicated/Private parity (schema compatibility only; no GA commitment for those environments in this launch).

---

2) Customer problem + why now

Customer pain we’re addressing:
- Updating models/configs is risky; teams want “safe change” mechanisms without building their own traffic splitting + rollback + auditability.
- Teams need rapid rollback when latency/error rate regresses.
- Regulated customers need approvals and audit trails for who changed what.

Why now:
- Hosted usage has crossed the threshold where “manual version flip” is a reliability and support burden.
- Beta partners have validated demand and uncovered operational edges (split mismatch, stalled step on metric timeout) that are now addressed.
- This strengthens Redwood’s “production-first inference” positioning: serving economics + safe operations.

---

3) Positioning (internal + external)

Primary positioning statement:
“Hosted Canary Rollouts let you safely introduce a new model version or configuration by gradually shifting production traffic, with guardrails, auditability, and fast rollback—built into Redwood Console.”

Key differentiators to emphasize:
- Production-grade guardrails (step size + soak time + approvals + auto-stop/rollback)
- Deterministic cohorting (predictable splits; easier debugging)
- Integrated observability: baseline vs canary metrics, in the same Console experience
- Governance: audit events and customer-visible rollout timeline

What we should NOT promise in GA messaging:
- “Automatically finds the best model” (no bandits)
- “Prevents all regressions” (it reduces risk; customers still own evaluation/validation)
- “Works for Dedicated/Private” (future roadmap; avoid accidental commitments)

Suggested short description for docs / release notes:
“Create percentage-based canary rollouts on Hosted routes with configurable step plans, approval gates, and automatic stop/rollback on SLO breaches.”

---

4) Target users + use cases

Who:
- ML engineers / platform engineers operating production LLM endpoints
- Engineering managers accountable for reliability and change control
- Security/compliance stakeholders (audit log evidence)

Top use cases:
1) Model version update with confidence
- Move from v1 → v2 of the same model (or a tuned variant) with 1/5/25/50/100 rollout
- Watch p95 latency and error/timeout rate; auto-pause if regression

2) Config changes (quantization, batching, caching)
- Safe introduction of an optimization profile (lower cost, unknown tail latency impact)

3) Region-specific risk management
- Roll out gradually while watching region dashboards (and avoid “global flip” surprises)

4) Governance / approvals
- Require a separate approver to progress past a threshold (e.g., >25%)

Who is out-of-scope for the initial GA:
- Customers needing full CI-quality gates with automated eval harness integrated as a strict block
- Customers wanting multi-variant experiments beyond baseline/canary comparison

---

5) Packaging, eligibility, and access model (GA proposal)

Feature availability:
- GA: Hosted routes only
- Gated behind feature flag at tenant level initially (staged GA). After stabilization, move to plan-based entitlements.

RBAC (expected/target):
- “Rollout creator” can create drafts and propose plans
- “Rollout runner” can start/pause/rollback within guardrails
- “Rollout approver” can approve gated steps / overrides (see policy)

Notes:
- Policy enforcement must be consistent across UI and API responses (clear error messages, actionable remediation)
- Ensure audit logs include actor identity (human or service account), role, and request correlation ID where applicable

Open question to finalize before GA comms lock:
- Do we message “enterprise feature” or “available on Pro+”? (Need final input from Product + GTM; avoid rework in docs)

---

6) Rollout sequencing (internal GA rollout plan)

Phased enablement plan (recommended):

Phase 0 — Internal dogfood (complete / ongoing)
- Redwood internal tenants and staging/prod shadow routes
- Validate cohorting stability and stop-condition wiring

Phase 1 — Beta design partners (complete / winding down)
- Limited set of tenants enabled manually via feature flag
- Weekly check-ins; escalate issues via dedicated Slack channel + support workflow

Phase 2 — Staged GA (first 2–4 weeks)
- Enable for additional tenants by request (“GA, staged enablement”)
- Default safe guardrails enforced; discourage overrides unless SRE-approved
- Monitor alert volume, cohort metric correctness, and support ticket trends

Phase 3 — Broad GA
- Default enablement for all eligible plans/tenants
- Self-serve in Console (no ticket)
- Formalize SLOs + oncall playbook for issues

Kill switch / backout strategy:
- Owner: Connor O’Brien (release) + Mina Haddad (data plane) for emergency disable
- Kill switch should: prevent new rollouts from starting, optionally freeze existing rollouts at current step (TBD), and revert routing to baseline if required
- Ensure a documented “rollout disable” runbook exists and is tested

---

7) Customer communications plan

Goals of comms:
- Explain what canary rollouts are (in Redwood terms) and when to use them
- Provide a clear “how to” for Console workflow
- Set expectations around guardrails and auto-stop behavior
- Provide troubleshooting steps and where to get help

Primary channels:
1) Docs update (required)
- Concepts: baseline vs canary cohorts, deterministic cohorting, step plans, guardrails
- How-to: create rollout, start, pause, progress step, rollback
- Troubleshooting: why a rollout paused, how to interpret metrics, what to do if split seems off

2) Console release notes
- Short announcement + link to docs
- “Known limitations” section (keep tight)

3) Email to current beta partners
- Thank you + GA details + any changes from beta defaults

4) In-product callout (optional, staged GA only)
- Small banner/tool-tip in Rollouts section for eligible tenants

5) Sales/support enablement note
- Internal one-pager + FAQ
- Link to runbooks and escalation process

Messaging blocks (draft copy snippets):
- “Safely roll out model changes with percentage-based traffic splits, built-in guardrails, and fast rollback.”
- “Automatically pauses or rolls back when error/timeout/latency thresholds breach (configurable by policy).”
- “Full change history: customer-visible rollout timeline + audit log events for governance.”

Comms timing:
- T-7 days: docs final review + support enablement session
- T-2 days: beta-partner email and internal #eng-releases announcement
- T0: release notes + docs publish + staged enablement begins
- T+7 and T+21: internal status update on adoption/support load; decide to broaden enablement

---

8) Internal enablement (Sales, Support, SRE)

Support readiness:
- Add macro/KB entry: “How do I do a percentage rollout on a Hosted route?” (tie to SUP-48211)
- Ensure support can answer:
  - Why did my rollout pause?
  - How do I rollback?
  - How do approvals work?
  - Where do I see baseline vs canary metrics?

SRE readiness:
- Dashboards: baseline vs canary cohort comparisons per route + region
- Alerts: stop-condition triggers should page the right oncall (avoid storms)
- Runbook: “rollout stuck or bad split” including diagnostics and escalation

Sales readiness:
- Competitive framing: “safe rollouts + governance” as a production feature
- Common objections:
  - “Do you have change approvals / audit logs?” → yes
  - “Can I gate rollouts on quality?” → partial/optional now; automation later

---

9) Responsibilities (RACI-ish)

Product:
- Marissa Cole: final scope, Console UX acceptance, go/no-go recommendation
- Paula Mendes: guardrails/stop conditions requirements, success metrics

Engineering:
- Dylan Brooks: Console + orchestration readiness; incident response liaison for Console/backend
- Mina Haddad: data plane traffic splitting enforcement readiness; kill switch behavior validation
- Ethan Park / Jordan Lee: policy engine and control plane enforcement correctness; RBAC mapping

SRE/Infra:
- Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: oncall readiness, paging correctness, runbook sign-off

Security:
- Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei: audit event schema sign-off, retention/export messaging sanity check

Docs:
- Elliot Price / Wei Chen: docs + troubleshooting publish; coordinate with release notes

Release management:
- Connor O’Brien: feature flag plan, staged enablement schedule, change management checklist, release comms coordination

Launch coordination:
- Soojin Lee: this brief, comms calendar, tracking open items to GA

---

10) Success metrics (first 30–60 days)

Adoption:
- # of tenants enabled (staged GA vs broad)
- # of rollouts created / completed
- Completion rate without manual intervention

Reliability + safety:
- # of auto-pauses / auto-rollbacks (and % that were true positives)
- Incidents related to split correctness (target: zero Sev-1; rapid mitigation for Sev-2)
- “Time to safe state” after breach detection (pause/rollback latency)

Support load:
- # tickets about rollouts (trend line)
- Top ticket categories (split mismatch, confusion about approvals, understanding metrics)

Performance observability health:
- Metric/tag cardinality stays within agreed budgets
- Dashboard query performance acceptable for top tenants

---

11) Known limitations / guardrails to communicate (internal + docs)

- Canary rollouts are supported for Hosted routes only (not Dedicated/Private).
- Cohorting is deterministic; traffic split is approximate at low volumes (small sample sizes).
- Streaming and retries: cohort stickiness is best-effort; see docs for retry semantics.
- Stop conditions are SLO-signal based (error/timeout/latency). Quality gates are optional/manual inputs for now.
- Some policy constraints are non-overridable (hard safety rails); other constraints may be overridable by approvers (final policy TBD).

---

12) Risks + mitigations

Risk: Split mismatch perception (customer expects exactly X% at all times)
- Mitigation: set expectation: “approximate,” show confidence interval/sample size hints, document deterministic assignment + sampling effects
- Mitigation: add diagnostics view (routing logs / cohort counts) and support playbook

Risk: Rollout gets stuck due to metric evaluation timeouts or telemetry delay
- Mitigation: orchestrator timeouts + retries; clear UI state and actionable error; safe default is “pause”

Risk: Alert storms / noisy auto-rollbacks
- Mitigation: conservative default thresholds during staged GA; tune per region/tier; add “minimum data” requirement before evaluating

Risk: Governance concerns (audit logs incomplete or unclear)
- Mitigation: security sign-off checklist; audit event examples validated against customer asks (fintech/security review)

---

13) Launch checklist (condensed)

Product/UX
- [ ] Console wizard UX approved (edge cases + destructive confirmations)
- [ ] Empty/error states reviewed

Engineering
- [ ] Feature flag and kill switch tested in staging
- [ ] Migrations completed + rollback tested
- [ ] E2E tests passing in CI; flaky test plan in place

SRE/Telemetry
- [ ] Cohort dashboards live
- [ ] Alerts configured and routed; tuning plan documented
- [ ] Runbook published and oncall trained

Security
- [ ] Audit event schema verified; sample events reviewed
- [ ] RBAC/approvals validated across roles

Docs & Support
- [ ] Docs published
- [ ] Support macros/KB updated
- [ ] Internal FAQ shared to #support and #sales-engineering

Go/No-Go
- [ ] PM + Eng + SRE + Security sign-off

---

14) FAQs (internal)

Q: What happens when auto-stop triggers?
A: Default behavior is to pause or rollback depending on policy configuration; Console should show the triggering metric and threshold, and record it in the timeline/audit logs.

Q: Can customers override a guardrail?
A: Only where policy allows, and typically requires an approver role. Some rails are intentionally hard-blocked.

Q: Is it safe to enable for all tenants immediately?
A: Recommendation is staged enablement for 2–4 weeks to validate telemetry correctness, alert volume, and support burden.

Q: Are we promising Dedicated/Private?
A: No. We are keeping schemas compatible to reduce future migration pain, but GA scope is Hosted.

---

15) Open items / decisions needed (as of 2025-03-20)

1) Packaging/entitlement decision (plan tier + whether approvals are enterprise-only)
Owner: Marissa + GTM (needs final by docs lock)

2) Kill switch behavior for in-flight rollouts (freeze vs revert to baseline)
Owner: Connor + Mina + Sean

3) Final default thresholds for auto-pause/rollback during staged GA
Owner: Sean + Aisha + Paula

4) Final wording for known limitations (streaming/retry semantics)
Owner: Elliot + Dylan + Mina
